description: Unofficial Bitwarden compatible server written in Rust, formerly known as bitwarden_rs

sources.entry: Vaultwarden - Lightweight Bitwarden server API implementation written in Rust. GPL-3.0 Rust/Docker

summary.one_liner: Vaultwarden is an unofficial, lightweight server implementation of the Bitwarden Client API written in Rust, compatible with official Bitwarden clients and intended for self-hosting.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a nearly complete implementation of the Bitwarden Client API, covering the personal vault, Send, attachments, website icons and personal API keys. It also lists organization features (collections, password sharing, member roles, groups, event logs, admin password reset, directory connector, policies) and multi/two-factor authentication methods (authenticator, email, FIDO2 WebAuthn, YubiKey, Duo). Emergency access and a Vaultwarden admin backend are included, along with a modified web vault client bundled in the container images. The project is positioned as a lighter alternative to the official resource-heavy Bitwarden service. It was formerly named Bitwarden_RS and was renamed to avoid branding confusion with the official server.
use_cases: run a Bitwarden-compatible backend for official clients
lightweight alternative to the official Bitwarden server
store passwords, attachments and Sends for a family or small team
deploy a password vault in Docker or Podman
enable FIDO2, YubiKey or Duo two-factor login on a self-hosted vault
how_to_run: docker run --detach --name vaultwarden --env DOMAIN="<your-url>" --volume /vw-data/:/data/ --restart unless-stopped --publish 127.0.0.1:8000:80 vaultwarden/server:latest
Alternatively, create a compose.yaml with the vaultwarden/server:latest image, a ./vw-data/:/data/ volume and port 127.0.0.1:8000:80, then start it with Docker Compose
Put a reverse proxy with HTTPS in front of the server (the web vault requires a secure context)
notable: Compatible with official Bitwarden clients, including mobile, desktop and browser apps
Covers many Bitwarden features such as Organizations, Send, Emergency Access and multiple 2FA methods
Ships a Vaultwarden admin backend and a bundled modified web vault
Formerly known as bitwarden_rs; renamed to separate from the official server
caveats: The web vault requires HTTPS and a secure context for the Web Crypto API, so a reverse proxy or TLS setup is recommended
Not associated with Bitwarden, Inc.; the maintainers provide no liability for data loss and recommend regular backups
Community-built packages may lag behind the latest version or deviate in configuration
